title: Croatoan
subtitle: The Roanoke Colony · North Carolina, 1587–1590
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, a 16th-century English colonial settlement in the coastal maritime forests of Roanoke Island in North Carolina in the late summer of 1590, weathered wood palisade walls, thatched-roof cottages, salt marsh cordgrass, loblolly pines, hazy humid mid-Atlantic coastal light, melancholy and uncanny, period 1590 detail, cinematic wide composition, fine film grain, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: In fifteen eighty-seven, more than a hundred English settlers landed on Roanoke Island, off the coast of North Carolina.
beats.img: A wide view of a 16th-century English colonial settlement with weathered wood palisade walls and thatched-roof cottages in a coastal pine forest, hazy humid summer light, distant salt marsh, melancholy, no people.

beats.vo: Their governor sailed for England for supplies. War delayed him for three years.
When he returned, in fifteen ninety, the colony was abandoned. The houses had been dismantled. There were no bodies. There was no sign of attack.
beats.img: An empty cleared area inside weathered 16th-century wood palisade walls where houses once stood, low stumps and overgrown grass, hazy coastal summer light, distant pine forest, desolate, no people.

beats.vo: Carved into a palisade post, one word: Croatoan. Carved into a tree, the letters: C-R-O.
beats.img: Close on a weathered wooden palisade post with the faintly carved letters CROATOAN in period 1590s English hand, dim coastal forest light, documentary still, eerie, no people.

beats.vo: The settlers were never found. The colony is now four hundred years old, and still unanswered.
beats.img: An empty wide coastal North Carolina salt marsh at dusk with distant pine forest, faded orange sky reflected in still water, vast and unresolved, no people.
